title: Codify API-native vs agent-harness model adapter seam
description:
Problem
Eshyra needs to support both clean API-key model adapters and subscription-backed agent-harness adapters.

The pure API approach is architecturally preferred: Eshyra owns prompt assembly, tool transport, tool execution, turn management, replay, diagnostics, and model-call lifecycle. However, API-key usage is likely too expensive for day-to-day development and may also be too expensive for normal gameplay. Subscription-backed adapters using Claude Code / Codex-style agent harnesses are therefore required for affordable development and probably affordable play.

Design Decision
Maintain separate adapters by vendor and auth/transport mode rather than pretending API-key and subscription-backed paths are equivalent.

Examples:
- Anthropic API-native adapter: API key, lower-level Anthropic Messages/tool API, Eshyra-managed tool loop.
- Anthropic Agent SDK adapter: Claude subscription/Claude Code transport, Agent SDK MCP tools, agent-harness-managed loop bridged into Eshyra.
- OpenAI API-native adapter: API key, lower-level OpenAI Responses/tool API, Eshyra-managed tool loop.
- Codex SDK adapter: ChatGPT/Codex subscription transport, Codex MCP tools, agent-harness-managed loop bridged into Eshyra.

PR #241 is the first concrete candidate implementation of the agent-harness mode, pending the turn-auditor/tool-obedience fix.

Explicit Tradeoff
We accept that tuning prompts, tool use, diagnostics, and turn management for subscription-backed agent harnesses may have unintended effects on pure API adapters that are not continuously live-tested, because API-key costs are prohibitive. Subscription-token usage is expected to be orders of magnitude cheaper in practice than equivalent API-billed usage. The codebase must reduce this risk through a clear model-call abstraction, capability declarations, deterministic tests, debug logs, and documentation, but we do not require expensive live API smoke tests for every change.

Auth Rule
Auth mode must be explicit and mutually exclusive. Subscription-backed adapters must not silently inherit or prefer API keys when a subscription/OAuth path is selected. If both ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are present, the selected provider mode must decide explicitly which one is used. Subscription mode must sanitize child SDK environments or fail fast if API-key precedence cannot be prevented.

Scope
1. Write an ADR documenting:
   - API-native adapters are the preferred clean architecture.
   - Subscription-backed agent-harness adapters are intentionally supported for affordability.
   - API-native and subscription-backed adapters are separate provider modes, not interchangeable auth variants hidden behind one class.
   - Fenced-text tool calling is not a supported gameplay protocol.
   - A provider is supported for gameplay only if its adapter can expose Eshyra tools through native API tools or harness-supported MCP/native tools.
   - Subscription gameplay calls, including primary DM calls, auditors, retries, and recaps, must stay on the subscription-backed adapter unless the user explicitly selects API billing.
   - The accepted testing/cost tradeoff: subscription paths will be exercised more often than API-key paths.
2. Update README/provider documentation with the same distinction in user-facing terms.
3. Refine the model-call abstraction so it uniformly represents both adapter families:
   - provider/vendor
   - auth mode: api-key vs subscription/harness
   - transport/client: Anthropic Messages, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI API, Codex SDK, etc.
   - tool transport: api-native, agent-mcp, unsupported
   - turn loop owner: Eshyra-managed vs provider-harness-managed
   - capability flags for gameplay support
   - debug fields for provided tools, forwarded tools, observed/executed tool calls, auditor calls, and provider/harness errors
4. Use the finalized Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter from PR #241 as the reference agent-harness implementation once it both exposes tools and enforces required mechanical tool use.
5. Extract or document the reusable seam rather than reimplementing the Claude adapter.
6. Preserve or define the clean seam needed for future API-native adapters.
7. Create or update follow-up beads for:
   - Anthropic API-native adapter if not already present
   - OpenAI API-native adapter
   - Codex SDK MCP subscription adapter
   - removal/containment of any remaining fenced-text gameplay path

Acceptance Criteria
- ADR exists and captures the API-native vs agent-harness adapter decision and cost/testing tradeoff.
- README/provider docs describe supported provider modes and their tradeoffs.
- Model adapter interfaces or metadata make auth mode, transport, tool transport, and turn-loop ownership explicit.
- Released gameplay cannot silently proceed with tools provided but no native/MCP forwarded tools.
- Claude Agent SDK MCP path is the reference implementation for agent-harness adapters.
- Debug logs clearly distinguish API-native and agent-harness calls.
- Debug logs clearly distinguish primary model calls, auditor model calls, retries, and recap calls.
- Subscription-backed gameplay does not silently use API-billed calls for auditor/retry/recap work.
- Fenced-text tool calls are not presented as a supported gameplay fallback.
- Codex implementation is not included in this bead except as a documented follow-up.

Non-goals
- Do not implement the Codex adapter here.
- Do not implement every API-native provider here.
- Do not remove every fenced-text code path repo-wide unless trivial and in scope.
- Do not require live API-key smoke tests as a merge gate.
